title: Standby playpad — escalation sprint (Harper)
body:
Purpose
- Quick personal scratchpad to prep for day-of escalation standby / customer sprint. Lightweight, copyable snippets and checks so I can run a 1:1, triage, and handoff without opening 5 different tabs.

Activation / triage thresholds (notes to self)
- Trigger if customer reports: total request failure (5xx) hitting >1% error rate for 10m, or latency P95 > 2s above baseline for 15m, or data exfil suspicion.
- Initial response timeline: ack within 10m, triage comms + initial mitigation plan within 30m, War-room (if needed) within 60m.

Quick checklist (first 30m)
- Slack: @oncall + #inc-urgent and ping customer-success lead (cc: account owner). Use simple template below.
- Get essential context: customer name, env (prod/dedicated/private), model, endpoint, approximate start time, recent deploys.
- Check metrics: request rate, error rate, latency distribution (P50/P90/P95), GPU utilization, autoscale events.
- Identify rollback or fallback options: pin to previous model version, route to lower-capacity region, enable cached responses.
- Create triage doc (this file copy -> add notes), create JIRA if not present (INC-xxxx).

Slack templates (copy/paste)
- Initial ack to customer: "Thanks — I've opened an incident (ID: INC-xxxx) and I'm assembling a triage team now. We're looking at request/error/latency signals and will follow up in 30 minutes with next steps. —Harper (SRE)"
- Internal loud ping: "@here INC-xxxx: customer X seeing elevated 5xxs on /v1/generate (prod, us-east1). P95 latency +2.8s. Need runtime + infra owners. ETA: 30m triage. Harp"
- Handoff to on-call: "@oncall: can you collect logs from cluster redwood-dedicated-42 and enable debug logging on route /v1/generate for next 15m? If we confirm model OOM, prepare to pin to v1.14 (previous)."

Who to call/DM (roles)
- Primary: eng-sre on-call (Ethan Ruiz) — infra, autoscale, routing
- Runtime lead: Maya Patel — kernel selection, quantization artifacts
- Platform owner / account: Jules Kim — customer comms + contract constraints
- Exec on-call: Priya (if SLA breach or legal exposure)
- Customer Success contact: Tara Singh (account owner)

Triage timeline (template)
- 0–10m: ack + collect basic signals + create incident ticket
- 10–30m: triage signals, reproduce locally if possible, try quick mitigations (route fallback, pin model)
- 30–60m: decision point — escalate to war-room if customer impact still high; prepare exec summary
- 60m+: war-room or maintain watch with rolling updates every 15–30m

Immediate actions to consider (fast wins)
- Toggle routing policy to fallback pool (lower-cost but stable) for affected customer
- Increase autoscale min for the instance group servicing customer
- Enable degraded-mode: short-circuit long-running pre/post-processing
- Revert last deploy if timing aligns with incident start and tests indicate regression

Data & commands I use first
- k8s: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=serving --selector=customer=<id>
- logs: logs-prod-collector query "service: serving AND customer:<id>" --last 30m
- metrics dashboards: perf/redwood/serving -> set time window to incident start
- cache check: redis-cli -h redis-prod get prefix:<customer>:cache-miss-rate

Customer-facing script snippets (use plain language)
- If it's latency (non-deterministic): "We see higher latency on your endpoint and are actively routing requests to a more stable pool while we investigate. You may see slightly different response times briefly; this is to restore overall throughput. We'll update you in 30 minutes with details."
- If it's an error surge: "We are investigating an increase in failed requests. As a temporary mitigation, we will route your traffic to a compatible model variant and monitor closely. No data has been deleted; we're focusing on availability."

Post-meeting / Post-handoff action items (template)
- Owner, action, due (48h unless urgent), notes
  - Harper: collate timeline and attach APM traces to INC-xxxx (due 24h)
  - Maya: verify kernel path & quantization config for model X; add regression test (due 48h)
  - Ethan: write short autoscale incident postmortem draft (due 48h)
  - Jules: customer email draft + next steps (due 24h)
  - CS: schedule follow-up call if customer requests longer-term review (due 72h)

Open questions / things to follow up
- Was there a model swap/optimization pushed ~incident start? Check deploy logs and PRs.
- Any correlated infra noisy neighbor events in the region? Need cluster owner confirmation.
- If we routed to fallback variant, did quality regress measurably? Attach eval snippets.

Notes-to-self (shortcuts & reminders)
- Keep messages short in Slack — avoid speculative root cause in customer messages.
- Always include incident ID in subject and first line of messages.
- If customer is on Dedicated/Private, involve platform eng early (networking, peering).
- For Private deployments: checklist includes KMS audit + call with infra team.

Handoff checklist for next shift
- Short summary + hypothesis (1–2 sentences)
- What we changed (routing, pin, revert)
- Observed effect metrics (before/after P95, error rate delta)
- Next immediate action and owner
- Links: logs query, dashboard snapshot, PR/deploy id, INC ticket

Quick copy snippets (for my notes doc)
- "INC-xxxx: initial triage shows P95 up from 1200ms -> 4200ms between 11:02–11:18; errors spike 1.6% -> 7.3%. Rolled back model to v1.14 at 11:38; customers now at 1.3% errors."
- "Action: Maya to run kernel debug on model v1.15 within 24h; Ethan to validate autoscale cooldown settings."

After-action doc outline (post-incident)
- TL;DR (2 lines)
- Timeline (minute level)
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (traces, logs, config changes)
- What worked (mitigations)
- Action items + owners + deadlines
- Follow-up: regression tests, config guardrails, monitoring alerts tuned

Personal reminders (mental)
- Breathe. Keep comms calm and repeatable.
- Use this file as the basis for the incident notes I'll paste into Confluence later.
- Keep ownership clear; if I assign someone in Slack, also add them explicitly to the Jira ticket.

TODO (short, immediate)
- [ ] Copy this file into incident folder when activating (Confluence draft placeholder)
- [ ] Create INC ticket with baseline metrics and attach dashboards
- [ ] Ping Maya and Ethan with quiet DM if they're not in initial Slack pings (avoid noise to channels)

End of scratchpad.

----

Version history notes (for me)
- 2026-03-10: created baseline playpad, cleaned up slack templates + timeline
- 2026-03-12: added private-deploy notes + post-handoff checklist (Jules feedback)
